featured_reviews.name: Vinit Vinayak
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Muthuswamy Cafe, and it was an amazing experience for anyone who loves authentic South Indian food.

The place has a simple yet comforting vibe, and the aroma itself sets the mood as soon as you walk in. The food is absolutely top-notch—fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. From crispy dosas to soft idlis and rich sambhar, everything tasted authentic and satisfying.

The service was quick and efficient, and the staff was polite and attentive throughout. It’s one of those places where you go for the food and end up loving the whole experience.

If you’re in Dadar and craving real South Indian flavors, this spot is definitely worth visiting!

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Fulsundar

Mutuswami Cafe is located just outside Dadar East railway station, so it’s very easy to find and perfect for a quick stop after travel. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, which is nice if you want to sit comfortably or just grab something quickly.
We tried the strawberry milkshake & mango milkshake both were thick, chilled, and refreshing. The paper masala dosa was big, crispy, and came with good chutney and sambar. Kanchipuram idli was soft and flavourful, a little different from regular idli and worth trying.
Cheese tava rice was spicy, cheesy, and filling good if you’re very hungry. We ended with pineapple sheera, which was warm, slightly sweet, and had a nice fruity taste.
Overall, it’s a good place for South Indian food and quick snacks near the station.

featured_reviews.name: Gayatri
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re in Dadar and craving authentic South Indian flavors any time of the day, Muttuswami Cafe is the place to be!
This is the only café in the area open 24/7, making it a perfect spot for early breakfasts, late-night cravings, or casual meetups at any hour.
The food quality is outstanding, with every dish served fresh, flavorful, and satisfying:
Cheese Pav Bhaji – perfectly buttery with a generous layer of melted cheese that elevates the classic taste.
Podi Idli – soft, bite-sized idlis coated beautifully in spicy podi masala and ghee.
Muttuswami Special Benne Dosa – rich, crispy, and soaked in butter with a delicious traditional touch.
Spring Dosa – a unique fusion twist, crispy outside with a flavorful stuffed filling inside.
Fruit Custard Dessert – creamy, refreshing, and loaded with fresh fruits for the perfect sweet ending.
Their fresh juices are equally impressive — especially the pomegranate juice and the orange-mosambi mix, both refreshing and naturally sweet.
What truly makes the experience special is the warm and polite staff. The service is quick, attentive, and always delivered with a smile. The beautiful interiors create a clean, cozy, and welcoming atmosphere, making you want to sit back and enjoy your meal.

Thank you so much for your wonderful review! We're thrilled to hear that you enjoyed the authentic South Indian flavors and that our 24/7 availability suits your needs perfectly. Your kind words about our staff and ambiance truly mean a lot to us. We can't wait to welcome you back for more delicious moments!

I had Daal Paalak Chawal, Mushroom crispy and chaas (Buttermilk).
Daal Paalak chawal was bland and was giving me taste of coriander more than daal or Paalak.
Mushroom crispy was typical desi chinese as mushrooms were made into pakores (bhajiya) and we're dipped in desi chinese coloured tangy sweet supposed to be chinese sauce!
It also had options of veg thali which I felt like tasting if at all I come here again by any random chance.
That thali had Vermicelli kheer (I was obviously peeking into other's tables and hence I know)! May be it's tasty , may be it's not! If anyone tries that, let me know!
Chaas or the Buttermilk was looking so thick and it was surprisingly so watery.. 🙊🙊 it was a nice jeera milky water i must say!
Ambience: premise is Nicely lit but it was hot inside. Really very hot and humid where outside weather was pleasant! So eating in hot and humid environment in a restaurant where I am paying for food and taxes as well is not my thing!
No washrooms in this restaurant, there is a public washroom in front of this!
This is right opposite to Sewree bus depot.
Card payments were accepted.
In and all, if I am to go again I would definitely hesitate unless am dying of hunger!

featured_reviews.name: vru
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Udupi Shri Krishna Restaurant, which is conveniently located just a 1-minute walk from Matunga East Railway Station—making it extremely easy to reach without any hassle.

I learned that the restaurant was inaugurated by Sane Guruji, which adds a nice historical and cultural touch to the place.

When we arrived, we had to wait in the coupon queue, but it was quite smooth. Within about 10 minutes, our name was called. Considering it was a Saturday, the waiting time was very reasonable. I’ve heard that sometimes the wait can go up to 45 minutes to an hour, but we were lucky.

The staff at the counter was very polite and attentive. One thing that stood out was how they reminded everyone to wash their hands before eating—such a small yet thoughtful and caring gesture.

The food is served on a banana leaf, which adds a traditional and authentic feel. The entire meal felt fresh, simple, and very much like home-cooked food.

The thali included:

2 sabjis
1 koshimbir (cucumber salad)
Roti and puri
Curd
Pickle
Buttermilk
Nimbu rasam and regular rasam
Rice with ghee
One sweet (options like rasgulla, halwa, shrikhand, or gulab jamun)

Curd and sweets are limited, while the rest is unlimited.

The taste was excellent—especially the curd and nimbu rasam, which were absolutely delicious. The rasgulla we had was fresh, mildly sweet, and exceeded expectations.

The management and service were top-notch. The staff ensured that hot food was served in every round, which made the experience even better. Overall, it truly felt like having a comforting meal at home.

The full thali costs ₹300, and the mini thali is ₹200, which is quite reasonable for the quality and quantity offered.

My only suggestion would be to introduce a premium thali option at a slightly higher price, including a few more South Indian dishes for those who want to explore more variety.

Overall, a wonderful experience—highly recommended to everyone! 👍

If you’re looking for a spot where traditional South Indian soul meets a modern, aesthetic vibe, Malgudi in Lower Parel is a masterclass in culinary harmony. Curated by the legendary Shankar Mahadevan, the restaurant feels less like a typical eatery and more like a carefully composed melody—vibrant, comforting, and full of character.
The ambience hits you first; it’s thoughtfully designed with a clean, aesthetic appeal that makes it perfect for a relaxed weekend brunch or a stylish dinner.
The Food: From Classic to Creative
The menu takes you on a journey through Karnataka and beyond, elevating humble staples into gourmet experiences.
Podi Cheese Balls: The spice of the podi cuts through the richness of the cheese, creating a crunchy, gooey delight that’s hard to stop at just one.
Ghee Podi Thate Idli: This was a standout. The idli was incredibly soft, acting as the perfect canvas for the fragrant, nutty podi and a generous dousing of ghee.
Davangere Benne Podi Dosa: True to its roots, this dosa was buttery (*benne*) and crisp, with the podi adding a layer of depth that reminded us why this regional specialty is so iconic.
Mulbagal Legacy Cheese Masala Dosa: The addition of cheese modernized the legacy recipe without overshadowing the traditional masala. Beverages:
Mango Berry Matcha: A vibrant, fruity twist on matcha that felt light and refreshing—a great palate cleanser between the buttery dosas.
Coconut Cold Brew Coffee: Smooth and tropical. The natural sweetness of the coconut milk paired beautifully with the bold kick of the cold brew.
Desserts:
You cannot leave without trying the Filter Kaffi Panna Cotta. It’s a brilliant nod to South Indian coffee culture, with a silky texture and a deep caffeine punch. The Chocolate Pull-Up Cake added a bit of "Instagrammable" drama to the table—decadent, rich, and the perfect end for any chocolate lover.

Malgudi isn't just about the name behind it; the food truly speaks for itself. It captures the "Legacy" of South India while dressing it up for the modern Lower Parel.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

Ramashray in Matunga is one of those classic South Indian institutions that still feels properly “Bombay” – bustling, no-nonsense and absolutely focused on the food. I dropped in specifically to try their ghee podi Thatte idli and walked out very happy (and very full).

The ghee podi Thatte idli is easily the hero of the menu. The idli itself is thick and soft – that perfect Thatte style – with a beautiful fermented flavour. It comes drenched in ghee, with a generous ring of podi that clings to every bite. The texture, temperature and seasoning were spot on; this is the kind of dish you could reorder without thinking twice.

The pineapple sheera was another standout. Warm, fragrant and not cloyingly sweet, with enough pineapple to cut through the richness of ghee – it felt like a proper old-school dessert, the kind you’d expect from a place that’s been doing this for decades. If you have a sweet tooth, this is non-negotiable.

Where the experience dipped a bit for me was the masala dosa. For a place with Ramashray’s reputation, I expected a benchmark dosa, but it was underwhelming:
•	The dosa was small in size compared to typical Matunga standards.
•	The texture lacked crispness – instead of that satisfying crunch, the dosa kept crumbling even when handled gently, which made it messy and not very enjoyable.
•	The masala itself was decent, but the base failed to carry it.

Service is fast, efficient and very typical of old-school South Indian joints in Mumbai – you’re seated, served and cleared quickly, which works well given the constant rush. Prices are reasonable for the quality, and the overall vibe is nostalgic: crowded, lively, with conversations, steel plates and filter coffee aromas all blending into one.

Overall, Ramashray still deserves its cult status for certain dishes, especially the ghee podi Thatte idli and pineapple sheera, which I would come back for in a heartbeat. I’m giving it 4 stars only because the masala dosa – usually the litmus test at a South Indian eatery – fell short on texture and portion size. Fix that, and this would easily be a 5-star experience.

Appam with coconut stew is amazing as well. Especially the stew was so delicious. Mysore onion dosa feels rich in flavour and is prepared in pure ghee. Kanchipuram idli was a decent one and a bit sour. Paniyaram was a one-of-a-kind and is a must try. Cheese pav bhaji was not bad but failed to meet the bar raised by other food items. For desserts, you have to have the pineapple sheera and you can thank me later. A south indian cuisines is incomplete with the iconic filter coffee and the coffee here will not disappoint you. The service is super quick and they serve you unlimited Sambar and Chutney

This restaurant was hitting home-runs after home-runs and I was about to give this place the coveted 5-star rating when they committed a hygienic blunder. I found a small hair in their Pav. Hygiene is as important as the taste and had they not compromised on the hygiene, my search for the 5-starred restaurant would have ended today. But alas the search continues!!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Mani’s Lunch Home-
Since 2007, during my monthly early morning office tours, I make it a personal ritual to stop at Mani’s Lunch Home in Matunga East for breakfast. No matter how early the day begins or how packed the schedule looks, I always get down here first—it’s my way of starting the day on the right note.
Over the years, I’ve tasted nearly every item served here. But my usual favorites are the idli-vada, medu vada, and the classic sada dosa. The idlis are soft and fluffy, the vadas crispy and golden, and the dosa—light, thin, and perfectly roasted. Each dish is accompanied by hot sambar and fresh coconut chutney that bring out authentic South Indian flavors.
One of the best parts of Mani’s is their warm and generous service. The staff pours unlimited sambar and chutney on your plate until you gently say “enough.” This simple yet heartfelt gesture has become the USP (Unique Selling Point) of the place. It's not just about the food, but the love and hospitality that comes with it.
Once I finish my meal, I always end with a cup of their aromatic filter coffee. Whether you prefer it light or strong, Mani’s coffee is brewed to perfection—rich, bold, and served in traditional steel tumblers that enhance its charm. For health-conscious guests like me, they also offer sugar-free tea, which is light, refreshing, and perfect to start the workday with clarity and balance.
After breakfast, I continue with my day feeling satisfied and refreshed. That peaceful moment at Mani’s sets a positive tone for whatever work lies ahead.
Mani’s Lunch Home is not just a restaurant for me. It’s a monthly ritual, a memory lane of flavors, and a place where time slows down—where every bite takes me back to the roots of comfort and tradition. In a fast-moving city like Mumbai, Mani’s is a calm, soulful corner that never changes.

featured_reviews.name: Ram Subramanian (Ram)
featured_reviews.review_text: Manis lunch home has always been my favorite spot from my college days in Matunga.On a Sunday I had some work in Matunga so decided to visit Manis lunch home . I am visiting this restaurant after a gap of 4 years. I ordered Idli vada sambar while my wife ordered lemon rice.The idli vada sambar was very good compared to all the ones I tasted in & around Mumbai. It was very close to the taste in southern part of India. In my college days visit to this restaurant made me nostalgic.As usual even after 24 years they still maintain the restaurant neat & clean. They still serve unlimited sambar & chutney with the dishes.I loved their chutney more than their sambar.The taste of idli vada was same as that tasted four year/ even 24 years before.It was always difficult to get a place to sit inside the restaurant during weekends especially the peak hours. Today we went at an odd time of 11 am so we could comfortably sit inside the small restaurant.The lemon rice was served with kerala pappadam & chutney. It tasted good. The rice looked bulky similar to that used in Kerala.Overall it tasted good.Then although my stomach was full I wanted to taste their plain dosa to which I am a bigger fan.The dosa taste amazing good & kudos to the team for maintaining their standards over the years. I topped it with a nice filter coffee. The coffee was great & a must have so whenever you have food here pls keep space for the filter coffee. My wife is a tea lover so she ordered Tea. The teas was good as per her. I did not want to spoil my coffee taste😜 so did not taste the tea.I love to keep the  taste of filter coffee to stay in my mouth as long as possible.It was nice to recollect old memories sitting in this restaurant. It had made our day.Thanks to the management to keep the restaurant intact even after so many years. Hats off to the team.It is a must visit restaurant in Mumbai if you like authentic South Indian breakfast.

They have self service and each dish is served with coconut chutney, tomato chutney and sambar.

Recommended items:

1. Podi Dosa – A simple yet outstanding dosa coated with aromatic podi and ghee, giving it authentic flavour.

2. Benne Podi Dosa – Soft on the inside, crispy on the outside, and generously layered with white butter and podi, making it rich and satisfying.

3. Thatte Idli – Large, pillowy-soft idli with a light texture that practically melts in your mouth.

4. Medu Vada – Perfectly crunchy on the outside and soft, fluffy, and airy on the inside.

5. Filter Coffee – Strong, aromatic, and authentic South Indian filter coffee with a rich coffee flavour.

A great place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic South Indian food without spending too much.

Cafe Madras is one of the most iconic South Indian restaurants in Mumbai and truly lives up to its reputation. Located in the heart of Matunga, this place is famous for serving authentic and delicious South Indian food with consistent quality for decades. The moment you enter, the aroma of fresh filter coffee, ghee, and spices creates a warm and nostalgic feeling.
I tried their famous dosa and idli, and both were excellent. The dosa was perfectly crispy with a flavorful potato filling, while the idli was soft, fresh, and served with tasty chutneys and sambhar. Their filter coffee was another highlight — strong, aromatic, and refreshing. Despite being crowded most of the time, the service is quick and efficient, which is impressive.
The restaurant maintains cleanliness and has a simple yet traditional atmosphere that adds to the experience. Prices are also reasonable considering the quality and popularity of the food. Overall, Cafe Madras is a must-visit place for anyone who loves authentic South Indian cuisine. It perfectly combines taste, tradition, and quality, making every visit memorable.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This is one of my all time favorite south indian spot . From Filter coffee to idli ,dosa everything here is really good. First as usual we ordered filter coffee which was amazing. Rava dosa was really crispy & dosa Jain mysore dosa here comes with green chutney. Next we order some jain Tomato uttapa which was amazing. Next order some medu vada served with some sambhar & coconut chutney. Next we vegetable toast sandwich which was also really good.  last but not the least we ordered some idli sambhar & rasam vada.
Everything here was very tasty & good.

Pro tip :
Always reach here early around 7-7.30pm as they have a long wait usually for 45 mins to 1hr to get a table.

Next if you have elderly people with you make sure to take a table downstairs & stairs to their upper floor our very step & can be hard for them.

And if you like pudla sandwiches then order their club sandwich which is equally good.

featured_reviews.name: vishal mahasukh joshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
A very cozy old Mumbai character place for authentic south indian food. For me the "feast" started with single idli vada dip in piping hot sambar with fresh coconut chutney. Followed by crisp golden roasted Rava masala dosa. I asked for the masla (alu sabji) seperately to maintain the crispness of the dosa till last bite. Again served with sambar, tomato chutney and coconut chutney...the version of dessert here was a first time experience for me here. A slice of bread with neatly trimmed edges, golden roasted in sumptuous butter and sprinkled with brown sugar ... Perfect blend of bit salty and sweet taste with those sugar granules bursting and dissolving in your mouth when they are partially warm. That was an indulging experience...and you think it's over?
Coffee served in small "pyali and katori" to close the perfect deal...
Overall one of the best lunch I had in a company of a very good friend, who introduced me to this place at the first instance.
All served with a smile on face.
If in this part of Mumbai, don't miss the opportunity.

featured_reviews.name: chirag shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Authentic South Indian Taste in the Heart of Matunga!

Udipi in Matunga truly stands out for serving one of the most authentic South Indian meals in the area. The food tastes homely, fresh, and full of flavour — from the perfectly crisp dosas to the soft idlis and that classic filter coffee which completes the meal beautifully.

What makes it even better is that the entire restaurant is fully air-conditioned, making dining here a pleasant experience even on hot days. The place is clean, well-maintained, and comfortable for families as well as groups of friends.

The service is quick, polite, and efficient — exactly what you’d expect from a traditional Udipi restaurant.

If you’re looking for genuine South Indian food in Matunga that combines great taste, comfort, and a welcoming vibe, this is definitely one of the best spots to visit. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Anchal Garg
featured_reviews.review_text:
A decent restaurant to try some authentic South Indian food 🥘 at a reasonable price.
Firstly, we had to wait for our turn so we waited in the queue for 15-20 minutes. Their service is lil slow as they took sometime to prepare the dosas but the taste was not compromised.
The dosas were crisp and the sambhar tasted good. Not too spicy and the appropriate amount of sourness.
It was on my bucket list to cover all the famous South Indian joints in Matunga, and it one is well covered. A must try for the crispy dosas and filter coffee ☕️

featured_reviews.name: Arvind Nadkarni
featured_reviews.review_text: Legendary & Authentic, no-frills Manglorean/konkani menu. Well prepared & served. Takes some waiting during peak hours(lunch & dinner time). Big hit with local gujrati's who throng for Dosa,Idli sambar. Recommended "Sambar Bhat", unlimited thali & the pana "vido" to finish off a sumptuous meal. No parking! Walkable from Matunga(east) Stn. Bang on the Maheshwari udyan circle.Prepare for a long wait during lunch &dinner hours, but well worth the wait!

I don't expect to spend 1000 Rs+ at a restaurant and experience street food like hygiene. Amazing food, but horrible service.

The service was quick and polite, and the staff made sure everything was clean and comfortable. The ambiance was simple but pleasant, giving a nice traditional vibe.
Overall, great value for money and a must-visit if you love South Indian food. I’ll definitely be coming back!
